mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% signals a supply-side shock without labor slack, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days due to input cost pressures.
regime_hint: tight labor market with supply shock
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase (PAYEMS) below 100,000 while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is rising signals labor market softening, which tends to precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 100,000 AND UNRATE > previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not negative in at least 70% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% within a single month, in the absence of a concurrent GDP contraction, signals an emergency easing that boosts risk appetite and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change < -1% AND GDPC1 YoY change > -2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) exceeding 5% while consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is above 3% suggests households are saving rather than spending, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days due to lower consumption demand.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals strengthening manufacturing activity, which tends to coincide with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in non-inflationary regimes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero during periods of sustained INDPRO growth in low inflation regimes (t-test p > 0.05).
